children: Jordan is preparing a pipeline of public-private partnership (PPP) projects worth nearly $10 billion to be implemented over the next three to four years as the government seeks to accelerate economic growth, Jordan News and other local media outlets reported on Wednesday.
These investments span water, energy, transport, infrastructure and public services, the media reports said, quoting Minister of Industry, Trade and Supply Yarub Al-Qudah.

The flagship schemes highlighted by the minister included the National Water Carrier Project (Aqaba-Amman Water Desalination and Conveyance (AAWDC) project), which is considered critical to Jordan's long-term water security, and a natural gas pipeline linking the Risha Gas Field to demand centres across the kingdom.
Al-Qudah said the pipeline is expected to raise Jordan’s natural gas self-sufficiency rate to around 80 percent by 2028.

The minister also highlighted the Airport City Project, which aims to create an integrated urban and economic hub to accommodate population growth, reduce the pressure on capital Amman and create new economic and development opportunities.

The latest plans are broadly in line with announcements made last year. In December 2025, state news agency Petra quoted Prime Minister Jaafar Hassan as saying that the government intends to tender $10 billion worth of projects before the end of 2026, with completion planned between 2028 and 2030. These included the National Water Carrier project, the Aqaba-Shidiyah/Ma’an-Ghor al-Safi Railway, the Al-Risha Gas Pipeline, Amra City as well as public transportation, energy, health, infrastructure projects.

The report had noted that the government allocated 250 million Jordanian dinars ($352.61 million) in capital expenditure for the National Water Carrier over the next four years and approximately JOD100 million ($141.05 million) for the Al-Risha Gas Project over the next three years.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
